rationale.conceptual: Standard but non-trivial method: X-ray diffraction data reduction, reciprocal-space mapping, and Lorentzian peak fitting require careful implementation and domain understanding (e.g., strain calculation, line-cut extraction). The method itself is not novel, but correctly applying it to this specific dataset with multiple conditions demands attention to detail.
rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline: data download, indexing, unit-cell refinement, strain calculation, diffuse scattering map reconstruction, line-cut extraction, and Lorentzian fitting. Requires integrating crystallographic software (DIALS, pyFAI, etc.) and handling raw image formats, multiple output artifacts, and conditional dependencies. Non-trivial orchestration and data assembly.

difficulty.reasoning: The task involves a multi-step crystallographic data reduction pipeline on synchrotron diffraction data, requiring domain-specific indexing, diffuse scattering analysis, and quantitative Lorentzian fitting. The pipeline is non-trivial in both domain knowledge and software orchestration, though the core methods (unit-cell refinement, linear regression, curve fitting) are established. Execution complexity arises from handling multiple strain/temperature conditions, reconstructing reciprocal-space maps, and integrating crystallographic tools.

compute_estimate.reasoning: CPU-only analysis of ~10 GB of raw diffraction images; memory footprint mainly for image processing and map reconstruction (few GB), large dataset volume drives data download needs.
